summary: Batch canonical message ordering keys in groups of at most 128

replay.detail: No replay or projection rebuild is introduced.

schema.detail: No table, index, trigger, claim kind, digest or version changes.

rules.detail: The earliest sent or desired claim, canonical kind-index lookup, numeric time, writer, sequence, batch, native minimum record position and legacy position rules are unchanged. Authority checks and wake decisions remain in their existing paths.

compatibility.detail: All message views and duplicate occurrences are retained, with stable canonical ordering. Missing earliest claims or batches still refuse without selecting a younger claim. Every key is gathered before sorting, so an error leaves the input vector unchanged. The non-text claim ID diagnostic remains column 5. When multiple faults coexist, SQLite step errors may change which error is reported first; identical diagnostic precedence is not promised. Each group observes one statement snapshot rather than one per message; different groups can still observe different cuts.

downtime.detail: One stable prepared statement reads keys for at most 128 supplied messages, replacing a statement per message on repeated work-wake history reads. Empty input issues no key statement. Exact statement-count, canonical parity, duplicate, boundary, error, reopen and indexed-plan controls are included. They do not establish CPU, latency, VM work at scale, a production cause or an idle SQL budget result; the next production phase capture follows deployment.

manual.detail: No new manual steps or configuration.

recovery.detail: This reader writes no persisted state. Source rollback restores per-message key reads without a data migration.
